lens: INTEGRITY AND AUTHORITY ARCHITECTURE — is root_lineage independence, hash-pinned ground truth, and the externally anchored seal real and reachable; are guardrails 7a/7b CI-gated; and is this architecture the right priority for being the best auditor.
verdict: The authority architecture exists as validators, not as a system. The three legs of goal §2 are each implemented as a pydantic model that can reject bad inputs — a same-root predicate (evidence_seal_authority.py:148), a documentary lineage manifest that correctly groups cogito under the DeepSeek root, a 24-case corpus with per-case provenance pins — but no leg has an issuer, an external anchor, or a consumer in the path that audits contracts. The seal builder has zero callers in src/; the "transparency proof" is a Merkle tree computed in-process from caller-supplied leaves; the OpenTimestamps client is imported by nothing the CLI can reach and has no header verifier. Lineage independence is enforced only inside the benchmark runner; the audit pipeline decides finding status from a regex over model-ID strings (config.py:2132) and operator-typed sha256 lineage literals in TOML, and the development path — the only path that has ever audited real code — compares model-ID strings and hardcodes NOT_ESTABLISHED at 16 sites. Guardrails 7a/7b are not CI-gated: CI is workflow_dispatch-only, the twelve release gates contain no lineage or provenance gate, and the 35-gate autonomy inventory has no gate for either guardrail. Meanwhile the architecture has been made unable to express success by type (721 Literal[False] fields; completed_real_audits le=0; unsatisfied_gate_count ge=1; freshness and baseline hardcoded UNEVALUABLE) and the ledger design converts any provider 429 into a permanent human gate. Against that, the one real engagement shows the detection failures were context failures (single-file manifests producing false Highs, 37/68 dependency-missing claims SUPPORTED by both reviewers) and provider-behavior failures (an 18-token empty response recorded as a clean result) that the integrity layer neither prevented nor detected. From this lens the codebase is not moving toward the goal: it is building an increasingly elaborate custody chain around a benchmark verdict over 13 KB of synthetic snippets that nothing consumes, while the audit product's authority — whether a High is real — rests on 2-of-2 unanimity between two reviewers reading the same truncated context. The design is the right shape for "no model self-qualifies"; it is the wrong priority for "best auditor", and its costs (brittleness, ledger poisoning, governance rebinding, typed impossibility) are now the dominant blocker.

claims.claim: The externally anchored seal (goal §2 clause 3) has no issuer and no external anchor: nothing in src/ or scripts/ calls build_evidence_sealed_authority_evidence or build_evidence_authority_subject; the 'transparency proof' is a local Merkle prefix over caller-supplied leaves with a caller-chosen log id; the OpenTimestamps transport is unreachable from any CLI command and cannot verify a Bitcoin header.
claims.evidence: grep -rln 'build_evidence_sealed_authority_evidence|build_evidence_authority_subject' src scripts tests → only src/mmaudit/models/evidence_seal_authority.py (definition), tests/unit/test_evidence_seal_authority.py, tests/unit/test_autonomous_benchmark_verdict.py. Local Merkle: src/mmaudit/models/evidence_seal_authority.py:1469-1476 (build_transparency_prefix_proof takes log_id_sha256 and authority_subject_sha256s from the caller), :1607-1623 (_subject_leaf_sha256 / _tree_root_sha256 computed in-process). Seal payload hardcodes durable_authority=False, authority_issuance_authorized=False: :1546-1556. cli.py and development_cli.py import none of opentimestamps_*, calibration_checkpoint*, calibration_calendar*, evidence_seal_authority (grep returns nothing). src/mmaudit/models/opentimestamps_replay.py:1-7: 'neither imports the reference implementation nor looks up a calendar, block header, clock… A claimed Bitcoin height is untrusted input'. docs/remediation/v3/autonomy_gate_inventory.json gate-external-transparency-seal: MISSING. tests/unit/test_evidence_seal_authority.py:586-590 asserts that no issuer API exists.
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: One small, verifiable anchor on the artifact a customer receives: sha256 of run-evidence-manifest.json submitted to an OTS calendar (or Rekor) at run end, the .ots receipt stored in the bundle, and an offline verifier that checks the receipt against an independently obtained block header / signed tree head. The anchor should be on the audit report, not on a benchmark verdict.
claims.recommendation: Delete the local Merkle 'transparency' concept and the calibration_* publication stack (~5,700 lines across models/opentimestamps_*, orchestration/calibration_*, opentimestamps_calendar_*). Ship a single `mmaudit seal <run-dir>` that stamps run-evidence-manifest.json via the existing httpx OTS transport (orchestration/opentimestamps_calendar_transport.py:142-290) and a `mmaudit verify-seal` that uses a vendored header verifier. Wire it into `mmaudit run` as the last step.

In the audit pipeline that actually reviews contracts, root_lineage is an operator-typed sha256 literal in TOML, consensus independence is a regex over the model-ID string, and there is no per-candidate 'same-root judgement voids it' rule — the falsifier/verifier selection never receives the candidate's originating lineage.

Consensus uses model_family: src/mmaudit/config.py:2132-2147 (splits the model id on '-','_','.' and keeps two tokens), consumed at src/mmaudit/orchestration/consensus.py:558 and :998-1001. Cross-exam rule only requires the two reviewers to differ from each other: consensus.py:361-379. Falsifier selection takes only config, not the candidate: src/mmaudit/agents/verifier.py:189-225 and :296-310. The documentary bridge into AuditConfig is dead: src/mmaudit/models/public_lineage_configuration.py:1-10 'deliberately does not mutate AuditConfig'; grep -rln public_lineage_configuration src/mmaudit returns no importer. candidate_review_stamping.py:27-40 stamps model_family, but grep for candidate_root_lineage/origin_root_lineage in pipeline.py, consensus.py, schemas.py returns nothing.
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: A single lineage source of truth (the documentary manifest) consulted at the moment a verifier, falsifier, cross-examiner or judge is assigned to a specific candidate, with the rule 'reviewer.root == candidate.origin.root → decision discarded' enforced in consensus.py and recorded per finding in findings.json.
claims.recommendation: Make consensus.py take the candidate's origin root (from candidate_review_stamping, replacing model_family with the manifest root) and void any verification/cross-examination decision whose root equals it. Load approved_model_lineages from config/public_model_lineage/manifest.json instead of TOML. Delete config.model_family.

claims.claim: The development path — the only path that has audited real code (125-file ForestRoadVault run) — has no lineage concept at all: reviewer distinctness is model-ID/alias string inequality, lineage_independence is a single-valued Literal at 16 sites, and the model actually used (z-ai/glm-5.3) has no entry in the lineage manifest.
claims.evidence: src/mmaudit/models/development_ensemble.py:71-79 _require_distinct_roles compares exact_model_id/canonical_model_id only; src/mmaudit/models/development_judgment.py:144-164 same. Literal['NOT_ESTABLISHED'] at development_ensemble.py:94,299; development_corpus_ensemble.py:69,299; development_corpus_judgment.py:186,504,553; development_judgment.py:244,478,510; benchmark/development*.py:66,147,178,614. grep -c 'glm-5.3' config/public_model_lineage/manifest.json → 0. Real-run evidence item 1: 317 claims, 216 two-reviewer SUPPORTED; item 2: two Highs and one two-reviewer-supported Medium later refuted by dependencies outside the manifest. claims.claim: Ground truth (goal §2 clause 1, guardrail 7b) is real and provenance-pinned only for 24 synthetic excerpts (median 489 bytes, 13 KB total); the 'public = established' half is refused by code and forbidden by the seal's compiled pin, and the 28-case product-benchmark fixtures leak their labels in source comments.
claims.evidence: benchmarks/model_corpus/provenance.json: 24 case_bindings, every origin.origin_kind SYNTHETIC_PLANTED, construction_basis PRECOMMITTED_NON_MODEL_FIXTURE, benchmark_scoring_authorized=false. Excerpt sizes measured: min 202, median 489.5, max 1011 bytes. Refusal: src/mmaudit/models/ground_truth_authority.py:403-407 raises 'public ground truth requires an independently verified publication capability' for any non-synthetic origin. Seal pin: src/mmaudit/models/evidence_seal_authority.py:1352-1365 requires case_count == 24 and origin_kinds == (SYNTHETIC_PLANTED,), so a public case would break the seal rather than extend it. Label leakage: 12 of 13 vulnerable files under tests/fixtures/solidity/maximum_assurance_protocol/src/ carry '// BENCHMARK: <bug description>' (e.g. AccessVault.sol:11 'intentionally missing owner authorization', ReentrantBank.sol:11) and SafeControls.sol:25,30 carry '// SAFE CONTROL:'. The 24-excerpt corpus itself is request-blinded (0/24 excerpts contain label words; only 3 prompt-injection canaries).
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: Hundreds of real, commit-pinned, publication-dated public findings (Code4rena/Sherlock/Immunefi class) with stripped fixtures, contamination controls, and a regression gate that fails when the corpus hash changes without a provenance update — authority over a 13 KB synthetic corpus proves nothing a customer will pay for.
claims.recommendation: Implement PublicEstablishedGroundTruthOrigin end to end (publication URL + report date + pre-fix commit + fixture stripped of comments), remove the 24/SYNTHETIC_PLANTED-only pin from the seal, and strip every '// BENCHMARK:' / '// SAFE CONTROL:' comment from fixtures the models see.

claims.claim: Guardrails 7a and 7b are not CI-gated as the goal requires: CI triggers are manual only, the twelve release gates contain no lineage-independence or corpus-provenance gate, four local gates return a constant blocker without executing, and the 35-gate autonomy inventory has no gate for either guardrail.

claims.claim: The architecture cannot express success by construction: authority is typed as impossible, so no run of any code path can terminate in 'authorized' or 'done' without rewriting the schemas, validator and inventory.

claims.recommendation: Convert every Literal[False] authority flag that the goal expects to become True into bool with a validator that requires the corresponding evidence object; remove le=0 / ge=1 bounds from governance schemas; delete the 'no issuer exists' test once an issuer exists.

claims.claim: The ledger's integrity property ('unknown billing blocks new work') is the mechanism that turned every provider transient into a human blocker in the real run: a 429 finalizes the row UNCERTAIN_ACCOUNTED at full reservation, the next reservation is refused, and the only escape is a two-row allowance compiled into source.

Development path: require_settled_prior_costs=True (development_budget.py:116-123) refuses on any RESERVED row; development_cli.py:639,761,935,1111,1300,1476 force maximum_attempts=1. Real-run item 5: ledger-5 $83.46 accounted / $29.37 settled, ledger recreated twice; item 4: operator rotated providers by hand 8+ times. Goal §5: 'abort at ceiling, never ask; per-call reconciliation recorded' — the ledger never reconciles a 429 because no generation-id settlement exists (cost_ledger.py _ENTRY_KEYS :39-51 has no generation id field).
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: Per-call reconciliation that settles to known cost via GET /api/v1/generation for every attempt (including failed ones, which cost $0), automatic same-model provider rotation on 429, and a ledger that carries a bounded conservative estimate instead of blocking.

Private-module imports at :5764-5769 (httpcore._async.connection, httpcore._async.http11, httpx._client, httpx._transports.default) and :6050-6051 (h11). Repo-wide: 956 'pristine', 1,206 '_TRUSTED_', 268 '__code__' occurrences under src/mmaudit. Same pattern in candidate_selection.py, candidate_plan_ancestry.py, generation_evidence.py, usage.py, route_constraints.py, authenticated_runner.py (~1,600 lines). This does not protect a customer from anything — a process that can monkeypatch can also edit the constants — and it makes every httpx release a potential silent loss of REAL evidence.

claims.claim: Integrity effort is concentrated on paths that do not decide findings. Custody, ledger and lineage machinery guard the benchmark/release bookkeeping; the audit pipeline that produces findings uses plain mkdir, a regex family for independence, and a finding-status rule whose only non-model evidence is a local fork reproduction that the reproduction subsystem cannot deliver on Linux or for callback/flash-loan exploits.
claims.evidence: src/mmaudit/orchestration/pipeline.py:4208 and :14221-14223 create run directories with plain mkdir (no directory_custody); directory_custody is used by release_*.py, forensic_export.py, calibration_*, development_* (30+ modules) but not the audit pipeline. Finding status: src/mmaudit/orchestration/consensus.py:381-441 — CONFIRMED needs quorum_verified (2 VERIFIED) AND a 'mmaudit-local-fork-reproduction' evidence fingerprint; otherwise NEEDS_REVIEW. Independence in the same rule is _has_exact_cross_examination (consensus.py:361-379) on root_lineage taken from config TOML (IA-02). Real-run items 1-2: the two false Highs and the refuted Medium were 2-of-2 SUPPORTED; the integrity layer recorded them faithfully and could not have flagged them because it measures identity and hashes, not whether the reviewer saw ReserveCascadeLib.
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: Integrity spend proportional to where a customer is harmed: whether a finding is real. That means context completeness (dependency closure) enforced as a hard gate before any reviewer opinion is labelled SUPPORTED, engagement gates on empty/short responses, and disagreement handling — before custody of the release ledger.
claims.recommendation: Move DEPCLOSURE/CONTEXTSRC to a hard precondition: a claim whose reviewer did not receive the closure of the primary file cannot be SUPPORTED. Add a per-response engagement predicate (tokens, per-surface records, reasoning tokens when requested) that re-dispatches rather than recording NO_CANDIDATES.

claims.claim: Identity integrity without behavioural integrity: the client validates exact model/provider/endpoint identity per response but has no engagement or variance gate, so an 18-token `{"findings": []}` from one provider is recorded as a clean NO_CANDIDATES result and exits 0.
claims.evidence: Endpoint identity validation is real: src/mmaudit/models/openrouter.py:25503-25611 (_validate_completion_envelope), :25893-25920 (endpoint_variant_mismatch). No engagement heuristic exists: grep 'engagement|empty.findings|zero.findings' over src/mmaudit hits only prompt text 'An empty findings list is allowed' (development_review.py:64, development_audit.py:86). NO_CANDIDATES exits SUCCESS: development_cli.py:1173-1175 only exits INCOMPLETE on status == 'INCOMPLETE'. Real-run item 4: same model (glm-5.3) on four providers gave 1, 2, 4, 5 claims on the same file; Together returned an empty list in 18 completion tokens while others spent 13-21k; a 10-file pass was discarded by hand.
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: Response admission that checks the model did the work (minimum completion tokens scaled to input, per-surface review records, reasoning tokens present when effort=high) and cross-provider variance measurement for the same model so a degraded endpoint is excluded automatically.
claims.recommendation: Add an engagement predicate to the response validator that classifies sub-threshold responses as DISENGAGED (not NO_CANDIDATES), re-dispatches to the next allowed endpoint, and records the variance per endpoint in the endpoint snapshot.

claims.claim: The candidate/judge route triple and the objective hash are compiled into pydantic Literal validators, so changing the goal text or swapping one endpoint breaks plan validation — integrity has been implemented as immutability of the code rather than of the evidence.
claims.evidence: src/mmaudit/models/candidate_selection.py:724-738 exact model IDs and provider endpoints (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813@together, z-ai/glm-5.2@deepinfra/fp4, moonshotai/kimi-k3@together) inside a validator; :985 objective_sha256 Literal equal to sha256 of product_completion_goal.txt; :225-230 required_reasoning_effort Literal['high'], distinct_root_lineages_verified Literal[False]. src/mmaudit/models/candidate_plan_ancestry.py:63-92 pins production ancestry to tests/fixtures/model_selection/*.json with hardcoded SHA-256 constants; :94-112 compiles two ledger rows citing an operator instruction.
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: Plans and pins live in signed/sealed data files; code validates shape, not values.
claims.recommendation: Move the route triple, objective hash and ancestry pins into the selection-plan JSON and validate them by hash against the sealed manifest, not by Literal type.

strengths: The same-root predicate and collision map are exact and tested: EvidenceSealLineagePair.same_root must equal root equality (src/mmaudit/models/evidence_seal_authority.py:148), the collision map is the exact candidate-by-judge product (:180-183), and a same-root judge voids the subject (:326-327; tests/unit/test_evidence_seal_authority.py test_same_root_judgment_voids_the_subject). This is the correct structural expression of 'no model self-qualifies'.

The documentary public lineage manifest is genuinely evidence-based and conservative: 17 captured HF model-card sources, 12 CONFIRMED / 4 UNCONFIRMED with reasons, and it correctly maps deepcogito/cogito-v2.1-671b to the DeepSeek root (config/public_model_lineage/manifest.json decisions: both → sha256:acc05797…) plus 8 conservative non-independence constraints (kimi-k2/k3, gemma/gemini, gpt-oss/gpt-5.6). Offline resolution refuses same-root and constrained pairs (public_lineage_authority.py:829-841).

The 24-case model corpus is request-blinded: 0 of 24 excerpts contain label words (only 3 deliberate prompt-injection canaries), every case has a provenance binding with construction file hashes and a regression-contract hash (benchmarks/model_corpus/provenance.json), and the runtime rebuilds every binding against compiled pins (ground_truth_authority.py:342-420).

Response identity validation is sound and was proven against a real provider in August: exact model in accepted set, exactly one selected provider, endpoint inside the allowlist, no fallback, diagnostic codes for every mismatch (openrouter.py:25503-25611, 25683-25920); `models discover` correctly failed closed on OpenRouter's duplicate exact routes for glm-5.2 in the real run (real-run item 4).

AtomicCostLedger is a correct fcntl-locked reserve→commit→reconcile design with duplicate-id refusal and cap enforcement (cost_ledger.py:488, 843, 901, 530-531, 371-375); the $250 ceiling is a hard bound and the real engagement spent ≈$33 settled. The defect (IA-08) is in the settlement policy, not the atomicity.

The authenticated runner path does build real AUTHSEAL inputs from live custody (orchestration/authenticated_runner_openrouter.py:1086-1123 → evidence_seal_authority.py:1685-2020) and a 1-case smoke has completed candidate+judge across three lineages (operator_results.md:5943) — the plumbing up to the seal issuer is exercised, not merely declared.

Every artifact is honest about its own status: NONAUTHORIZING, NOT_ESTABLISHED, MOCK vs REAL, 'findings are unvalidated defensive hypotheses' — the system never overstates authority it does not have, which is exactly the truthfulness property the product vision §4.3 demands.

lens: AUTOMATION — distance from "zero human blockers in the run"
verdict: From the automation lens the codebase is not converging on the goal; it is converging on an exhaustive, honest catalogue of why the goal is unmet. The product audit command (`mmaudit run`) cannot execute a single model call because the CLI never obtains the live model-selection/refresh/pricing authorities the pipeline demands and no non-test code can issue them; the qualification hand-off is a dead end by unconditional raise. The only path that has ever audited real source (`mmaudit development ...`) is self-labelled non-qualifying and, in the one real engagement, needed a human to build 125 one-file manifests by hand, rotate providers by hand 8+ times, drive ~10 passes because retries are hardcoded off, suffix run-ids to dodge ledger identity collisions, and recreate the cost ledger twice because a stranded RESERVED or UNCERTAIN row blocks every future reservation and no command can clear one. Of those, the manifests, rotation, retries, run-id collisions and ledger recreation are engine gaps; only the missing lock files and symlinked /tmp parent were operator-side mistakes, and even those were hidden behind one fixed refusal string. A tree-in/report-out run needs at least seven things that do not exist: a partitioner whose closure is reachable on real contracts, provider rotation with variance reconciliation, in-run retry with generation-id-backed cost settlement plus ledger recovery commands, an engagement gate on empty findings, typed failure reasons a supervisor can branch on, parallel shards with per-manifest time bounds, and a renderer that turns ensemble consensus into a report. Governance adds a further human loop: every operator relay append breaks the validator and therefore `make test` until Codex re-binds hashes, and the governance/inventory schemas cannot represent success at all (completed_real_audits le=0, unsatisfied_gate_count ge=1, nine Literal[False] authorities). The budget ceiling, secret transport and identity validation are genuinely automated and fail closed; everything between "tree" and "report" still has a human in it.

lens: COMPETITIVE POSITION — what the best smart-contract auditors of 2026 (Trail of Bits, Spearbit/Cantina, OpenZeppelin, Sherlock/Code4rena wardens, Certora, Cyfrin Aderyn, Olympix, agentic auditors) deliver that this engine does not, and where a fully automated cross-lineage ensemble could genuinely beat them.
verdict: From this lens the codebase is not on a trajectory to best-in-world; it is on a trajectory to a well-governed, mid-tier, single-pass LLM triage tool wrapped in an unusually rigorous evidence chain. The only path that has ever audited real code (the `mmaudit development` lane) is a one-file-per-request, one-attempt, no-tool model read with a five-class taxonomy whose prompt forbids "operational attack steps" and self-labels every output "unvalidated defensive hypotheses" (development_corpus.py:735-764); in its one real engagement it produced two High false positives from missing context and 0 Highs reaching consensus. The path that would compete with a firm — 22 specialist investigators, per-surface coverage records, cross-examination, PoC reproduction, fuzz/formal engines, evidence-capped consensus — is real code but no user can execute it (pipeline.py:4093-4098; cli.py:7510-7513; completed_real_audits=0). Against every peer category the engine currently lacks the table-stakes deliverables: exploit PoCs beyond `vm.prank`+`call` with scalar args, executed economic attack simulation, invariant proofs without an operator-authored Certora spec, any cross-chain differential review, mechanism-level remediation verification, and a public track record. Free deterministic tools (Slither, Aderyn) out-deliver the default `mmaudit scan` on a Solidity repo, which ships three Python-only Semgrep rules and Slither off. The places an automated ensemble could win — explicit per-surface coverage, reproducible sealed evidence, cross-lineage disagreement as signal, and a two-orders-of-magnitude cost advantage (~$33 settled for 125 files) — are either unreachable or, where measured, show provider nondeterminism dominating signal (median pairwise overlap of 1 root across five temperature-0 trials). The architecture's aspirations exceed any single firm's offering; the executable product today would not survive a head-to-head with a mid-tier boutique, let alone a contest leaderboard.

claims.claim: The only measured detection quality is far below any competitor and is dominated by provider nondeterminism, not audit signal.

claims.claim: Cross-lineage consensus, the goal's core authority mechanism and the ensemble's only potential edge over a single human reviewer, is currently a same-answer filter that does not analyse disagreement, does not verify root-lineage independence on the executable path, and did not remove context-blind claims in practice.

On the product path, consensus.py:361-379 only checks the two cross-examiners differ from each other, never from the candidate's origin lineage. Best-in-world would treat reviewer disagreement as a trigger for targeted evidence gathering (fetch the dependency, run the test), not as INCONCLUSIVE.

claims.claim: Where a fully automated cross-lineage ensemble could genuinely beat human firms — cost, explicit per-surface coverage, reproducible sealed evidence, and repeatability — the engine has the right skeleton but either cannot execute it or measures the opposite.
claims.evidence: Cost: operator evidence item 8, ~$33 settled for a 125-file two-chain audit plus three remediation verifications (firm engagements of that scope are typically five to six figures). Coverage: ModelSurfaceReviewRecord with reachability (schemas.py:3474-3486) and the surface-set enforcement at scheduler.py:6156 are stronger than any human report's coverage statement — but only on the blocked path. Evidence: forensic_export.py:345 export_complete_forensic_bundle and run_authority.py bind every artifact by hash, which no firm offers. Repeatability: operator_results.md:2526 median pairwise overlap 1 root at temperature 0 — the ensemble is currently less repeatable than a single human, and external anchoring (OTS/Rekor) is MISSING per autonomy_gate_inventory.json.
claims.what_best_in_world_requires: To beat firms the ensemble must convert its cost advantage into breadth (many lineages, many passes, full repository every time) while keeping precision, and must turn variance into signal via N-of-M stability plus deterministic tie-breaking; per-surface coverage and sealed evidence are then genuine differentiators no human team can match at scale.
claims.recommendation: Spend the unused ~$217 of the $250 ceiling on breadth and repetition on the synthetic corpus first: 4+ lineages x 3 passes, stability-gated claims, then per-surface coverage rendering. That is the one axis where automation can surpass humans; the current single-pass, single-file, single-attempt design forfeits it.

strengths: The finding schema and consensus rule on the product path are firm-grade: CandidateFinding (schemas.py:2806-2830) requires attack_path, preconditions, compensating_controls, false_positive_conditions, a verification_test and source/sink; consensus.py:381-441 refuses CONFIRMED without a reproduction fingerprint and refuses HIGH_CONFIDENCE without two exact VERIFIED verdicts plus an unguarded attack path — stricter than most human reports' evidence discipline.

Per-surface review records with mandatory reachability paths (ModelSurfaceReviewRecord, schemas.py:3474-3486) and a 22-role specialist catalogue with disjoint responsibilities (constants.py:47-70, agents/specialists.py) are a real design advantage over human coverage statements and over single-prompt agentic auditors — if made executable.

Truthfulness discipline is enforced in code, not prose: MOCK/UNVERIFIED execution evidence cannot be credited (openrouter.py:11238-11246; isolation/provenance.py:569-589), formal/dynamic results distinguish 'no counterexample within bounds' from proof (schemas.py:1453-1463), and NO_CANDIDATES/INCOMPLETE are never rendered as safe.

The fork-reproduction template's realism constraints (reproduction.py:1497-1516 forbidding vm.store/vm.etch/vm.warp/vm.sign in the attack phase; capability policy limits at reproduction.py:1323-1328) correctly encode the vision §15 rule that a PoC must not fabricate authority — the constraint is right, only the expressiveness is missing.

Cost per engagement is two orders of magnitude below a firm (~$33 settled for 125 files plus three verifications, operator evidence item 8) with a hard $250 ledger cap (cost_ledger.py), which is the economic basis on which an ensemble could out-scale human review.

Complete forensic bundle export with hash-bound run manifests (forensic_export.py:345, :515; verify-run at cli.py:5498) gives a reproducibility guarantee no human audit provides, and the evidence-seal/collision-map models (evidence_seal_authority.py:138-190) correctly void same-root judgement.

The Codex process adopted the three architectural fixes that the real engagement exposed (DEPCLOSURE, CONTEXTSRC, AUTOPARTITION) within hours and correctly rejected conflating provider diversity with lineage independence (operator evidence item 7).

lens: DETECTION CAPABILITY — does the engine find real bugs in real code at a quality a top human audit firm would respect (what models are asked, what context they get, dependency closure, cross-file reasoning, exploit reproduction, formal/fuzz integration, false-positive control, severity calibration)
verdict: On this lens the codebase is not moving toward the goal. Two very different auditors coexist. The one that has actually audited real code (the `mmaudit development` path) is a single-pass, single-primary-file LLM read with no compiler, no scanner, no test execution, a 5-class taxonomy, a finding schema with no preconditions/attack-path/reachability/false-positive fields, model-assigned severity that nothing calibrates, and two reviewers who see exactly the same (incomplete) context and answer SUPPORTED/REFUTED/INCONCLUSIVE on "the claim as written". Its measured performance is 8.9-13.3% per-pass root location and 8.8% structural precision on the planted dev corpus, and on ForestRoadVault both Highs were single-file false positives that two reviewers supported. The other auditor (the seven-pass product pipeline with blind shards, 27 specialist roles, verifier, anonymized cross-examination, falsifier, judge and an evidence ladder) is the one a firm might respect on paper, but `mmaudit run` cannot reach a real model (cli.py never supplies the six authorities pipeline.py:4093-4098 demands; the only producers are tests), so it has never been exercised outside FakeOpenRouter, and even by design it cannot CONFIRM the dominant DeFi exploit classes (no contract deployment/callbacks/arrays in the PoC DSL, operator-pinned targets, macOS-only fork execution) and it publishes the maximum severity any model assigned (consensus.py:891-897). The cross-file gap that produced the false Highs is being addressed by an untracked dependency-closure module whose CALL_CLOSED status is unreachable on any contract with a mapping, an internal call, or an interface call (verified offline on a 20-line vault), so automatic partitioning refuses real protocols and context still arrives either as one file or as the whole bundle per request. Finally, the ground truth on which the goal's "authority" would be earned is 24 excerpts of 202-1,011 characters scored by exact line range plus 28 toy contracts with `// BENCHMARK:` label comments — it cannot measure firm-grade detection and would certify a model that cannot audit. Detection quality is currently an operator-run, hand-reported measurement outside the product's own definition of an audit (completed_real_audits remains 0).

strengths: The product consensus ladder is sound in design: CONFIRMED requires two exact VERIFIED verdicts plus a local fork reproduction fingerprint, HIGH_CONFIDENCE requires two VERIFIED plus a complete unguarded source->sink path, high/critical additionally require two cross-examination decisions from two lineages, and everything else stays NEEDS_REVIEW (src/mmaudit/orchestration/consensus.py:381-441, :361-379).

Primary reviewers are blind to peers, cross-examination is anonymized and forbidden from inferring lineage (src/mmaudit/prompts/cross_examination.md:1-12), and every requested surface must get an explicit REVIEWED_NO_ISSUE/CANDIDATE/INCONCLUSIVE/NOT_REVIEWED record with a reachability path from an entry point (source_audit.md:20-30; ModelSurfaceReviewRecord enforcement schemas.py:3538-3572) — silent omission cannot become 'reviewed'.

The exploit-test and falsifier design explicitly guards against tautological PoCs ('A passing test must mean that the claimed security property was violated, not merely that a call completed', exploit_test.md:11-13; falsifier.md:2-4) and the financial-settlement reconciliation rule (exploit_test.md:22-28) is stricter than most firms' PoC standards.

Deterministic counterexamples can originate findings independently of models (CandidateOriginKind.DETERMINISTIC_EXECUTION with bound provenance, src/mmaudit/models/schemas.py:2836-2862) — the right architecture for non-LLM detection lineage, once engines are wired.

The development path is honest about itself: every artifact hard-codes findings_validated/audit_complete/qualification_eligible/release_eligible False (src/mmaudit/models/development_review.py:310-313) and the prompts label output 'unvalidated defensive hypotheses' (development_corpus.py:744-745); the closure module refuses (NOT_ESTABLISHED) rather than fabricating closure (dependency_closure.py:201-203, static closure shortfall taxonomy).

The reviewer prompt contains the right verification instinct — 'Follow references into supplied helper implementations before concluding that a guard is absent' and 'A repeated pattern or privileged design choice is not automatically an invariant violation' (development_corpus_judgment.py:75-77) — and the real-run shows reviewer 1 (Kimi) correctly using a supplied failing test to refute a resurrected concern when the multi-file manifest was hand-built.

Real quality numbers exist and were measured honestly on a planted corpus (root location, assertion, union across trials, precision: operator_results.md:2526-2558, 2669-2674, 2725), and the 09-14 operator analysis correctly traced the two false Highs to the single-file context gap and produced concrete tickets (DEPCLOSURE, CONTEXTSRC, AUTOPARTITION) that Codex adopted within hours.

lens: ENGINEERING HEALTH — maintainability, dead code, duplication, size vs. goal, refactor priority
verdict: From the engineering-health lens the codebase is not converging on the goal; it is converging on an ever-larger, ever-more-rigid refusal surface. Size is fighting the goal rather than serving it: the product's core path is one 9,928-line async method (pipeline.py:3971-13898, 835 locals, 30 closures) that has never executed against a real model; the provider client is a 10,951-line class whose largest function (4,437 lines) exists to hash the bytecode of httpx/httpcore/h11 internals; and the type system plus 192 generated schemas (355k lines, 9.5 MB) encode "not done" as 721 Literal[False] fields and 2,802 `const: false` values that validators refuse to let change. The dominant complexity (a floor of 21.6k lines, 24% of openrouter.py, 75% of authenticated_runner.py) is in-process anti-monkeypatch machinery defending against a threat model with no attacker, while the properties the real run actually needed — retry, parallel shards, distinguishable failure causes — are absent or structurally dead. Duplication has already drifted semantically (`_canonical_sha256` exists 52 times with 28 different bodies, 25 of them ASCII-escaping where the shared helper does not), layering is inverted (77 lower-layer modules import from orchestration/, 48 mutual-import pairs, 478 deferred imports), 26,916 lines are unreachable from any CLI command, `make test` fails at collection, and five days of work sit uncommitted. The builder's own throughput confirms the trajectory: of 121 commits since 2026-09-03, 18.2% of changed lines are product code versus 36.4% generated schemas and 93 commits touch only docs/. A human team could not maintain this without first deleting a large fraction of it; an autonomous builder operating under "never fabricate a result, continue with schemas/types/validation when blocked" (AGENTS.md:135-146) will keep growing it. Strict mypy, ruff, typed Pydantic models and fast offline tests are real strengths, but they verify the shape of refusals, not the existence of an audit.

lens: PROCESS — the Codex/operator/governance loop under docs/remediation/v3: velocity, what it optimises for, what it refuses, and whether its artifacts are product or governance
verdict: The process is fast, honest and does not converge on the goal. In the 29 days since the objective was frozen (f794db0, 2026-08-17) it produced ~206k committed plus ~39k uncommitted lines of product code, 1,558 worklog entries (112–178/day this week) and 49 ticket completions, yet not one goal-defining requirement advanced: A–V COMPLETE count went 11→12 (K, on 08-24) and has been flat since; the seven goal-critical tickets that were QUEUED at the freeze (QUALIFY, SINGLE-AUDIT, MULTI-AUDIT, BENCHMARK, CERTIFICATE, ADR, RELEASE) are still QUEUED; the unfinished ticket count rose 37→41 while 53 new tickets were minted; the qualified-path ledger has consumed $0.68 of $250 (0.27%) with exactly one 24-case attempt (08-27, $0.20, failed closed); main has not moved since the freeze and no product code has been committed since 09-09. The loop optimises for fail-closed refusal and hash-bound record custody (Literal[False] fields 96→721, 'pristine' guards 44→956 during v3), for test-identity counts as acceptance, and for reconciling its own mirrored records after every operator append — not for detection quality or for a user-runnable audit. Its success predicates are unrepresentable in its own schemas (completed_real_audits le=0, unsatisfied_gate_count ge=1, nine Literal[False] authorities, 104 test pins of 29/15), so 'done' cannot be reached without rewriting the governance code, and no ticket exists to do so. Every paid or real step is executed by a human, the builder never inspects the resulting private artifacts (recorded 'uninspected' 113 times), and the relay carrying real-run evidence is nonauthorizing by design, so run failures cannot become tickets without the human retyping them into Codex's session — five operational tickets and an engagement gate raised on 09-14 were neither adopted nor declined. Architectural tickets, by contrast, were adopted within 46 minutes and 'locally COMPLETE' within 12.5 hours — but completed to acceptance criteria that make the feature unreachable on real input (CALL_CLOSED cannot be earned without compiler provenance the closure never receives; AUTOPARTITION scale acceptance runs on a 12M-token fake endpoint and a one-function abstract contract). The artifacts this process produces are overwhelmingly governance (records, receipts, schemas, refusal machinery) rather than product, and on the current trajectory the human remains the scheduler, the executor and the only feedback channel — the opposite of the prime directive.

strengths: The loop never overclaims: every worklog entry and the handover state 'REAL 0', 'nine false authorities', 'not a qualified audit'; the objective text is hash-pinned (product_completion_goal.txt sha e3b895de…, checked by scripts/validate_governance_state.py ARTIFACT_PATHS) and the process refused to self-edit it (product_completion_goal.txt:1).

The validator does catch real drift: cross-mirror disagreement (validate_governance_state.py:383), frozen-history edits (:29-36, :353-362), fabricated accounting in the relay (:325-345), and a single active ticket (:375-389); `make governance` runs offline in seconds and exits 0 today ('Governance coordination valid: 43 unfinished tickets').

The operator relay is a genuinely useful, timestamped, hash-bound record of real-run evidence — 122 entries with reproducible commands, costs and ledger states (docs/remediation/v3/operator_results.md), which is how the 13% recall, provider variance and 18-token non-engagement facts exist at all.

Adoption of well-argued architectural proposals is fast and technically correct: DEPCLOSURE selected within 46 minutes (worklog.md:848) and completed with honest boundary statements (worklog.md:427), and the LEGDIVERSITY proposal was rightly rejected as not lineage independence (work_queue.md:1496).

Acceptance receipts are reproducible: each completion cites exact test-run identities, XML digests and independent readback (worklog.md:429-431), and failures are retained rather than deleted ('Failure preservation', worklog.md:433).

BLOCKED_TECHNICAL / INCONCLUSIVE / PARTIAL are used as intended (AGENTS.md:148-157); nothing in the record fabricates a provider result, and the one real 24-case campaign was allowed to fail closed at $0.20 rather than be forced (operator_results.md:5395-5420).

Budget discipline held: the qualified ledger is fcntl-locked, cap-bound and reconciled per call (src/mmaudit/orchestration/cost_ledger.py:488-1023), and total real spend across all ledgers is ~$46 actual / ~$110 accounted of the $250 envelope.
